sources.title: Sergei Tokhtas’ev: Cimmerians, Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.note: Direct academic article: chiefly eighth/seventh centuries BCE; uncertain cultural identification and language; Alyattes defeat late seventh/early sixth century. Reject imported1500BCE as founding date.

sources.title: State Archives of Assyria 1, letter 31: More on the Cimmerian defeat
sources.note: Indexed original scholarly edition: SAA01 031, ABL0197, K00181; clay tabletNineveh, Sennacherib toSargonII, reign721 to705BCE. Opening a-na LUGAL be-lí-ia = To the king, my lord. Obverse8 onward reports Urartian defeat. Direct502; query P334142 Cimmerian reproduces full indexed edition and metadata.

sources.title: State Archives of Assyria 10, letter 100: Astrological advice concerning Cimmerians
sources.note: Indexed original edition SAA10 100, BM99030, ABL0679+, reignAshurbanipal. Obverse27 identifiesUmman-manda/Cimmerians;28 onward solar eclipse and Jupiter; reverse1 scant rains interpretedasroyalgoodomen. Directtimeout; query Cimmerians SAA10 100 reproduces text.

sources.title: Sardis Expedition: The Lydians and their world, introduction
sources.note: Direct/indexed scholarly excavation publication: Gyges request for Assyrian aid against Cimmerians, diplomatic connection documented in Akkadian sources, note6.

sources.title: Zaur Gasanov: Early Iron Age horse-bits and cheek-pieces from Azerbaijan
sources.note: Direct2017 primary abstract: second half eighth/seventhBCE; bronze bits and three-hole cheekpieces; connections to bothScythian/Cimmerian cultures, not individuallyprovenethnicity.

sources.title: Leont’eva and colleagues: A proto-Maeotian horseman burial from Adygea
sources.note: Direct2025 primary abstract: discovered2023, lateeighthBCE, manover55, healedcranialinjury, equine/bronzegear; campaign link proposed, isotope results and nonhybridhorse findings. Clearly proto-Maeotian, not secureCimmerianethnicity.

sources.note: Direct objectrecord: circa650BCE,4.3cm,midseventhoccupationHoBoutsidewall; chape identification; largerrelatedroundelpossiblyunfinishedandlocalproductionhypothesis; notcertainmakerethnicity.

sources.note: Direct objectrecord: circa625 to580BCE uncertain,2.5cm,central tenon attachment; maker/styleScythianorCimmerianqualified.

sources.title: Penn Museum Digital Gordion: Chronology
sources.note: Direct excavation synthesis: old700BCECimmerianattributionrevised; radiocarbonfivebarley/lentil/flaxsamplesfromseparatepotsTerraceBuilding2A andtree-ringdating circa800BCE.

sources.title: Sardis Expedition: HoB Lydian III and its destruction level
sources.note: Direct/indexed excavation publication: formerKimmerianDestruction652BCEreappraisedafterCorinthianjugHoB355reclassifiedLateGeometric;nowlatereighthcenturyBCE.

sources.title: Wilkin and colleagues: Dairying enabled Early Bronze Age Yamnaya steppe expansions
sources.note: Direct full primary paper, 2021. Main text dates Early Bronze Age 3300 to 2500 BCE. Results: 15 of 16 individual Early Bronze Age calculus samples, ruminant species assignments, and lactose discussion. Avoid inconsistent horse-sample denominator and unsupported proof of riding.

sources.title: University of Helsinki: The Yamnaya Impact on Prehistoric Europe
sources.note: Direct research project: western distribution in Romania, Bulgaria, Serbia and Hungary; exchange, material culture and population dynamics. Imported outline is regional coverage, not a state boundary.

sources.title: Natalia Shishlina: Early Herders of the Eurasian Steppe
sources.note: Direct Penn Museum Expedition 2001 primary field synthesis. Use only Yamnaya discussion and explicitly regional Catacomb transition. Braided mats, seasonal lowland/highland evidence, bone pins; do not transfer later Catacomb grain, textiles or wagon model to Yamnaya.

sources.title: O. H. Shaposhnykova: Mykhailivka settlement, Encyclopedia of Modern Ukraine
sources.note: Direct NAS Ukraine excavation-author article, 2018. Middle and upper Yamnaya levels: metal, stone and bone workshops, stone walls and ditches. Do not transfer lower-level semi-subterranean houses and hearths into later levels.

sources.title: Justyna Rzońca: Wagons of Yamnaya community, evolution and influence
sources.note: Direct six-page primary conference paper, 2021, printed pages 13 to 18. Page 13: author collected 43 well-described wagon graves. Pages 14 to 16: dismantled wheels, chassis used as beds or covers, heavy four-wheel construction and Izobilnoe clay wheels. Hypothetical religious meanings not asserted.

sources.title: Morgunova and colleagues: Bioarchaeology of Childhood in the Yamnaya Culture
sources.note: Direct primary abstract, 2022, Boldyrevo-4 kurgan 1. Three children about six in two graves, 3300 to 3100 calibrated BCE, before imported map start. Mats differ and vessels share shape/decoration but not manufacture; related separate groups and inherited status are author interpretations. No speculative disease cause repeated.

sources.title: Haak and colleagues: Massive migration from the steppe is a source for Indo-European languages in Europe
sources.note: Direct authors’ 2015 research preprint abstract linked to Nature publication. Sampled German Corded Ware ancestry modeled about three quarters from Yamnaya-related source. Public copy omits universal ancestry percentages and distinguishes ancestry from language or political identity.

sources.title: University of Helsinki: Volker Heyd on studying the Yamnaya
sources.note: Direct university interview: no written source material for these communities; archaeological, biological and Indo-European linguistic methods. No global assertion that writing did not exist 5,000 years ago. No reconstructed sentence presented as an attested sample.

sources.title: Hosek, James and Taylor: Tracing horseback riding and transport in the human skeleton
sources.note: Direct full 2024 primary scholarly review. Coxofemoral changes and Other forms of animal transport sections: skeletal markers nonspecific; wagon travel is an alternative. Critique does not establish that no Yamnaya individual rode.

sources.title: Anthony, Trautmann and Heyd: Horse genetics, archaeology, and the beginning of riding
sources.note: Direct/indexed original 2026 abstract, Science Advances 12(20), eady7336, 13 May 2026. Authors argue for Yamnaya riding circa 3200 to 2600 BCE; treated as a position in a live debate, not universal agreement.
